narrative.overview: The portfolio is a working desktop, not a webpage dressed as a laptop. A visitor lands on a full-bleed Portfolio OS: the supplied violet ASCII-hands artwork on near-black, a translucent light menu bar, a dock, and a centered welcome window that names Bradley and puts the four live projects one click away. The two hands frame the welcome; the authored B lives in the chrome, not as a wallpaper glyph. There is no hardware frame; the screen is the page. The OS is the navigation and the proof. Work is a Finder-like project browser; Notes is About; Terminal is Skills; Mail is Contact; Web is the project page; About This Portfolio is the system card. Search, Apps, and Controls are original features with original names. The flat reader below the desktop is the accessible, no-JS, printable edition. The tone is calm, precise, and quietly playful: a real tool you can use, not a costume.
keyCharacteristics: The user-supplied violet ASCII-hands artwork on near-black, full-bleed and fixed.
Light windows by default; dark mode restages the windows, menu bar, dock, and tone colors while the artwork stays fixed.
The authored B lives in the welcome, menu bar, app icon, README file, favicon, and sleep screen.
White/graphite windows with red/yellow/green traffic lights; 11px corners; opaque content panes.
Translucent chrome only: menu bar, dock, Controls, notifications.
System UI type in the windows; one true-black Terminal in monospace.
Every interaction a visitor can see actually works: windows drag, apps open, Search finds, Terminal answers, contact links resolve.
Original naming and icons. No Apple logos, feature names, or product names.

rules.name: The Lit Desktop Rule
rules.body: Start with light windows. Dark mode restages the windows, chrome, and tone colors; the supplied artwork is the fixed ground in both modes.

rules.name: The One Black Room Rule
rules.body: The Terminal is the one true-black app surface. The artwork is a near-black ground, not a UI surface; every app surface is white, graphite, or a project tone.

rules.name: The Chrome-Only Blur Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur belongs to the menu bar, dock, Controls, and notifications. Content windows and the reader stay opaque.

rules.name: The Authored B Rule
rules.body: The B is an SVG path (B_PATH), never a font glyph. It appears in the welcome, menu bar, app icon, README file, favicon, and sleep screen, never as a watermark over the artwork.

rules.name: The No-Apple-Names Rule
rules.body: The features are Search, Apps, and Controls. No Apple logos, product names, feature names, or SF fonts.

rules.name: The Native Voice Rule
rules.body: Use the system UI face for the OS and the system mono face for the Terminal. No display webfont, no brand typeface, no second sans.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A project's type sits beside or below its name, never as a kicker above it.

rules.name: The Layer Rule
rules.body: A shadow describes a window above the desktop. If it reads as a glow, remove it.

rules.name: The No-Drag-Only Rule
rules.body: Dragging is never the only route to an action. Window → Move Left / Move Right / Center moves the active window from the keyboard.

dos: Do keep the supplied violet artwork full-bleed and fixed, with the welcome centered in the hands' gap.
Do keep the authored B path everywhere the mark appears.
Do keep the menu bar, dock, and windows working: drag, minimize, zoom, close, open, search, type.
Do keep the three ways into contact: Mail, the welcome's Say Hello, and the reader.
Do keep the original names Search, Apps, and Controls; never reintroduce Apple feature names.
Do keep the 24px minimum targets, 2px focus rings, keyboard routes, reduced-motion freeze, and no-JS reader.
Do keep the dark mode a full restaging, not an inversion.
Do keep the print stylesheet: white reader, desktop hidden, project URLs visible.
donts: Don't add laptop hardware, a notch, a keyboard deck, or a desk scene; the screen is the page.
Don't reintroduce the generated B wallpaper, contour rings, or pointer parallax.
Don't put content in glass cards, neon gradients, or a hero-and-cards layout.
Don't use pure black outside the Terminal or pure white as a page ground.
Don't use blur on content windows.
Don't put a kicker above a heading.
Don't make dragging, hover, or a pointer the only route to any action.
Don't invent clients, metrics, testimonials, a CV, or a live AI.
Don't use Apple logos, Apple feature names, or SF fonts.
